label: UniFi Dream Router 7
description: UniFi Dream Router 7 (UDR7) - 4x 2.5G RJ45 (1 PoE) + 1x 10G SFP+ (10G/1G). WiFi 6/7; 26 W max.

poe.note: 15.4 W, the whole published budget: the tech-spec table lists "2.5 GbE RJ45 = 4 (1 PoE)" and, under Hardware, "PoE Budget = 15.4W", "PoE = 15.4W", "Voltage Range PoE Mode = 44-57V" (read 2026-11-19). One 802.3af port at its 15.4 W maximum exactly uses the budget, which is why eth0 is the only poeOut port modelled. This model has no datasheet in its documents list - the product page names only https://ui.com/qig/udr7 (InstallationGuide) - so the rendered spec table is the vendor source.

notes:
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr7 (HTTP 200, 694,590 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered tech-spec table) says "Power Method = Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 1.5A Max, 50/60 Hz"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so eth1 / eth2 / eth3 now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

WiFi: the Dream Router 7 carries a tri-band 802.11be (WiFi 7) access point - the Integrated WiFi table on https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr7 (HTTP 200, 694,590 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered) prints "Throughput 6 GHz 5.7 Gbps / 5 GHz 4.3 Gbps / 2.4 GHz 688 Mbps" and "MIMO 6 GHz 2 x 2 / 5 GHz 2 x 2 / 2.4 GHz 2 x 2", "WiFi Standard 802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax/be (WiFi 6/6E, WiFi 7)". So radio0 = 2.4 GHz 688 Mbps, radio1 = 5 GHz 4.3 Gbps, radio2 = 6 GHz 5.7 Gbps. This model has no datasheet on dl.ui.com (https://dl.ui.com/ds/udr7_ds.pdf answers 302 to the marketing home page), so the rendered tech-spec table is the vendor source. `bands` is declared per radio: engine/media.js derives bands from the rate alone and a 4.3 Gbps 802.11be radio would otherwise claim 6 GHz as well.

Layer 2: Ubiquiti's controller device database classifies this SKU as a switch - https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, read 2026-11-21) lists UDR7 deviceCapabilities GATEWAY, SWITCH, ACCESS_POINT, NETWORK_APPLICATION, PROTECT_APPLICATION, CONTROLLER, APPLICATION_MODE, HAS_CLIENTS and draws its panel as `01 02 03 04 05` - and the vendor tech-spec table publishes the bridge's forwarding database at https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr7 (HTTP 200, 694,590 B, read 2026-11-21), which prints "MAC Address Table Size = 2,000" with "VLAN/Subnet-based Traffic Segmentation" ticked. No LACP row appears, so no LAG is claimed. A MAC address table is a bridge FDB; a gateway that only routed would hold neither it nor a LAG. While the row shipped without `l2-forward` its copper sockets were routed interfaces: `switchport access vlan 10` was answered with "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability", and two hosts on eth0 and eth1 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP ("not addressed to this device"). The page's WAN side is unchanged and still not pinned: "Default WAN Ports = (1) 10G SFP+ / (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45", "Max. WAN Port Count = 4", and the diagram is one unbroken run of five, so no copper socket is renamed WAN here.
